It's the process of loaning money that actually creates the new money and 90% of the currency in circulation is digital. Only about 10% of currency in circulation today is actual printed paper bills or metal coins. The majority of money being created from thin air happens at a local bank level.

When John Doe applies for a loan and is approved, the bank prints out the loan contract. When it's first printed, it's just a pile of paper. When John Doe signs the loan contract it becomes a "promissory note" just like fiat currency dollars. The value of that promissory note is equal to the amount of the loan, plus the total amount of interest that will accrue through the life of the loan. That is how the banks create money out of thin air.

It's commonly understood that when you take out a mortgage you'll end up paying back 2.5 times the amount of the amount borrowed. So if you borrow $100,000.00 to buy a home and make steady payments for 20 years, you'll end up paying back $250,000.00.

What's worse is that after John Doe signs the loan contract for $100,000.00 mortgage and it becomes a promissory note worth $250,000.00, the Bank can turn around and sell that mortgage contract to investors.

Picture this; let's say you want to buy a $200,000.00 home and you have 20% downpayment saved up. You go to the bank and give them $40,000.00. They take your $40K and add it to their balance sheet as an asset, they just made $40K. Then you sign a mortgage contract for $160,000.00 and it becomes a promissory note worth $400,000.00. The bank then places that promissory note value on their balance sheet as an asset worth $400K.

In just a few minutes the bank has added $440K to their balance sheet as new assets and they transferred some ones and zeros to the bank of the seller worth $200K. The bank just made $240K, if they hold that promissory note for the life of the loan. Or they can sell the promissory note worth $400K to an investor for $300K and let the investor hold it for the life of the loan. Now the bank ends up with positive assets of $40K, the downpayment, and the $300K from the sale of the promissory note minus the $200K they transferred to the seller. That leaves them with $140,000.00 profit if they sell the mortgage contract in less than a month.
